title: Grade 9 Biology National Exam & Practice 2015 (6 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 6 chapters (21 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: One of the following renowned Ethiopian biologists has developed a vaccine for the rinderpest disease.
options: Professor Yalemteshay Mekonnen
Professor Sebsebe Demissew
Professor Tilahun Yilma
Professor Beyene Petros
questions.explanation: Professor Tilahun Yilma developed the vaccine for rinderpest, a viral disease that affects cattle and other cloven-hoofed animals.

questions.questionText: A grade nine student has planned to study animal cells using a compound light microscope. She prepared a slide of stained human cheek cells for this purpose. Which one of the following activities should she first do?
options: Set up the microscope with the lowest power objective in place.
Adjust the iris diaphragm until the maximum brightness is coming.
Looking through the eyepiece lens to move the objectives down.
Using coarse focusing knob to rotate the nosepiece for a higher magnification lens.
questions.explanation: When using a microscope, the correct first step is to start with the lowest power objective lens to easily locate the specimen before increasing magnification.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about plant cells? They have
options: Lysosomes which contain hydrolytic enzymes.
Vacuole which controls all activities of the cell.
Cell wall which gives support and strength to the cell.
Chloroplast which is filled with sap, liquids and minerals.
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose that provides structural support and strength.

questions.questionText: A plant cell is placed in a solution which has lower solute concentration than its contents. After a few minutes the cell will become
options: Flaccid
Turgid
Burst
Plasmolysed
questions.explanation: When a plant cell is placed in a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration outside), water enters the cell by osmosis, making it turgid.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about human food digestion?
options: Mouth use protease enzyme to breakdown proteins.
The stomach physically breaks down the ingested food.
The small intestine is site of absorption of digested molecules.
Large intestine is the site of lipid hydrolysis.
questions.explanation: The small intestine is responsible for the absorption of nutrients after digestion, including amino acids, sugars, and fatty acids.

questions.questionText: Which of the following enzymes is correctly matched to the food stuff it acts on?
options: Maltase - lipids
Pepsin - protein
Trypsin - starch
Amylase - fats
questions.explanation:
Pepsin is a digestive enzyme found in the stomach that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.
 Maltase acts on maltose (a sugar), trypsin acts on proteins, and amylase acts on starch, not fats.

questions.questionText: Which of the following breathing movements happens when air enters into and exits from the balloon lungs in the bell-jar model?
options: Air enters when the rubber sheet is pushed up.
Air enters when the bell-jar thorax contracts.
Air exits when the balloon lungs have higher pressure than the external environment.
Air exits when Y-piece is rotated both clockwise and counterclockwise.
questions.explanation: In the bell-jar lung model, air enters the balloons (lungs) when the rubber sheet (diaphragm) is pulled down, creating low pressure inside. Air exits when the lungs have higher pressure than the external environment, causing exhalation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following structures of the heart is correctly matched with its function?
options: Left ventricle - contracts and forces oxygenated blood around the body
Right atrium - contracts and forces deoxygenated blood into the lungs
Left atrium - contracts and forces blood into the right ventricles
Right ventricle - contracts and forces blood into the left ventricles
questions.explanation:
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the rest of the body.
 The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, not to the left ventricle.

questions.questionText: Suppose your friend fails suddenly due to heart attack while he is playing football. The victim needs artificial breathing to keep him alive until medical support arrives. Which activity is strictly prohibited in this situation?
options: Open the airway by removing any obstacles from the mouth
Remove any obstacle from the mouth that might block the airway
Give mouth-to-mouth resuscitation if he is conscious
Make sure the airway is open and the head is tilted back
questions.explanation:
Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation should only be performed if the person is unconscious and not breathing.

 If the person is conscious, it is dangerous and unnecessary, so it is strictly prohibited.

questions.questionText: In the diagram showing blood circulation system in the human body, the parts indicated by numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4 are respectively:
options: Pulmonary artery, pulmonary vein, vena cava, aorta
Aorta, vena cava, pulmonary vein, pulmonary artery
Vena cava, pulmonary artery, aorta, pulmonary vein
Pulmonary vein, aorta, vena cava, pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: Blood leaves the left ventricle through the aorta to the body, returns via the vena cava, goes to the lungs through the pulmonary artery, and returns oxygenated via the pulmonary vein. Therefore, the correct order is: aorta → vena cava → pulmonary vein → pulmonary artery.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about the activities of the heart?
options: Diastole is when the heart muscles contract and force the blood out.
Systole is when the heart muscles relax and it fills with blood.
The noise of heartbeat one hears through a stethoscope is the sound of valves.
As the heart beats blood travels through the arteries with a uniform pressure.
questions.explanation: The 'lub-dub' sound of the heartbeat heard through a stethoscope is produced by the closing of heart valves — the 'lub' is due to atrioventricular valves closing, and the 'dub' due to semilunar valves closing.

questions.questionText: During culturing micro-organisms, all of the following activities are important EXCEPT:
options: sterilizing the inoculating loops.
transferring target micro-organisms into an agar medium.
tilting the lid of the  Petri dish during inoculation.
adding distilled water to a sterilized agar.
questions.explanation:
Sterilizing inoculating loops, transferring microorganisms into agar, and slightly tilting the Petri dish lid during inoculation are important aseptic techniques.

 However, adding distilled water to already sterilized agar is unnecessary and may introduce contamination.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases can be caused by more than one type of microorganism?
options: Typhoid
Tuberculosis
Cholera
Gastroenteritis
questions.explanation:
Gastroenteritis (inflammation of the stomach and intestines) is a general syndrome that can be caused by various pathogens, including different bacteria (like Salmonella or E. coli), viruses (like Rotavirus), or parasites.

 The other options are typically caused by a specific microorganism (Typhoid by Salmonella typhi, Tuberculosis by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and Cholera by Vibrio cholerae).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases is correctly explained with its causes or symptoms?
options: Gonorrhoea is caused by Treponema pallidum.
Syphilis has sore ulceration on the genitals as a symptom.
Syphilis is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Gonorrhoea has a burning sensation symptom while urinating.
questions.explanation:
Gonorrhoea is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and a key symptom is often a painful or burning sensation while urinating (dysuria).

 Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, and while it causes a sore (chancre), the first option incorrectly matches the cause of Gonorrhoea with Syphilis.

questions.questionText: The names of which two taxa are used in binomial nomenclature?
options: The highest and the lowest unit of classification
The two highest units of classification
The two lowest units of classification
The two middle units of classification
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature, the two-part naming system for organisms, uses the Genus and the Species names, which are the two most specific and therefore the two lowest units of the standard taxonomic hierarchy (Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> **Genus** -> Species).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following phyla is characterized by a flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure, that runs along the dorsal side of the body?
options: Phylum Annelida
Phylum Arthropoda
Phylum Mollusca
Phylum Chordata
questions.explanation: The flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure described is the notochord, which is a defining feature of the phylum Chordata.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following groups of organisms is correctly matched with its phylum?
options: Snail - Phylum Annelida
Earthworm - Phylum Mollusca
Starfish - Phylum Echinodermata
Fish - Phylum Arthropoda
questions.explanation:
Starfish belong to the phylum Echinodermata (spiny-skinned animals).

 Snail belongs to Mollusca, Earthworm to Annelida, and Fish to Chordata.

questions.questionText:
A zoologist studied 5 vertebrate species (spA, spB, spC, spD and spE) and described their features as follows: 

spA: Smooth moist skin; pass parts of their lives in water and on land. 

spB: streamlined body with scales; gills for gaseous exchange.

 spC: feathers over the body with scales on legs; endothermic; horny beak.

 spD: Dry skin covered by scales; lungs for respiration.

 spE: mammary glands; endothermic; high internal body temperature.

 Based on the features listed above, spA, spB, spC, spD and spE can be classified under the vertebrate classes respectively:
options: Pisces, Amphibia, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia, and Pisces.
Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, Mammalia, and Amphibia.
questions.explanation:
Based on the features:

- spA: smooth, moist skin; lives in water and on land → Amphibia

- spB: streamlined body, scales, gills → Pisces (fish)

- spC: feathers, beak, endothermic → Aves (birds)

- spD: dry scaly skin, lungs → Reptilia (reptiles)

- spE: mammary glands, endothermic → Mammalia (mammals)

questions.questionText: Which one of the following events happens during carbon cycle? Carbon dioxide is:
options: removed from the air by animals during respiration.
returned into the air by plants during photosynthesis.
transferred from plants to animals by their feeding relationship.
absorbed from air when microbes decompose plant and animals.
questions.explanation:
In the carbon cycle, carbon is fixed into organic molecules by plants (photosynthesis).

 This organic carbon is then transferred from plants to animals when the animals consume them (feeding relationship).

questions.questionText: Which of the following plant adaptation mechanisms helps cactus to adapt in the desert environment?
options: Having broad leaves.
Storing water in its tissue.
Spreading its seeds in wider areas.
Increasing number of stomata in its leaves.
questions.explanation: Cacti are succulents; their primary adaptation to the arid desert is the ability to store large amounts of water in their fleshy stem tissues.

questions.questionText: Consider the following diagram demonstrating the pyramid of energy. Which of the following is INCORRECT about the above pyramid of energy?
options: The organisms of the first trophic level convert light energy into chemical energy.
The organisms of each trophic level use large proportion of the energy to build their body.
The amount of energy transferred through the trophic levels drops with each step up of the pyramid.
The energy lost as heat to the surrounding in each trophic level is insignificant.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.
